TOUR.G11.T1.AIRPORTS.A1.title: Air travel concepts and South Africa's airports
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRPORTS.A1.description: Use air-travel terms (gateway, inbound, outbound, domestic, regional, inter-continental, long-haul, chartered) and identify South Africa's main airports, ACSA, the airlines that operate here and how to read an airline timetable.
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRPORTS.A1.strand: Term 1 — Transport services in South Africa
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRPORTS.A1.caps_topic: Tourism sectors — airports, airlines and airport operations
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRPORTS.A1.recovery_strategy: Re-teach the flight types using a South African departure board, then sort one flight example at a time.

questions.question: In tourism, what does the word 'gateway' mean?
options: A major entry and exit point into a country or region, such as a main airport
A locked gate at the entrance to a game reserve
A type of aircraft used only for cargo
The boarding pass given to a passenger
questions.expected: A major entry and exit point into a country or region, such as a main airport
questions.memo: A gateway is a main point through which tourists enter or leave a country or region — for example, OR Tambo International Airport is South Africa's busiest air gateway.

questions.question: What is a domestic flight?
options: A flight between two airports inside the same country
A flight that crosses the Atlantic Ocean
A flight between South Africa and another continent
A flight that has no fixed schedule
questions.expected: A flight between two airports inside the same country
questions.memo: A domestic flight stays within one country's borders, for example Johannesburg to Cape Town. It does not cross any international border.

questions.question: Which airport is South Africa's busiest international gateway?
options: OR Tambo International Airport in Johannesburg
Bram Fischer International Airport in Bloemfontein
questions.expected: OR Tambo International Airport in Johannesburg
questions.memo: OR Tambo International Airport (code JNB) in Johannesburg is the busiest airport in South Africa and on the African continent, handling the most passengers and flights.

questions.question: True or false: Airports Company South Africa (ACSA) operates South Africa's major airports, including OR Tambo, Cape Town and King Shaka.
questions.memo: ACSA owns and operates nine of South Africa's main airports, including the three largest: OR Tambo (Johannesburg), Cape Town International and King Shaka (Durban).

questions.question: A flight that covers a very long distance and takes many hours, such as Johannesburg to New York, is called a _________ flight.
questions.memo: Long-haul flights cover long distances and last many hours (usually more than six). Short-haul flights are short trips, and medium-haul flights fall in between.

questions.question: Which airline is South Africa's national carrier?
questions.memo: South African Airways (SAA) is the country's national carrier (the airline that represents the country). Emirates, British Airways and Lufthansa are international carriers that operate flights to South Africa.

questions.question: A flight from Johannesburg to Windhoek in Namibia, a neighbouring country, is best described as a:
questions.memo: A regional flight travels between countries in the same region — for South Africa that means nearby Southern African countries such as Namibia, Botswana or Zimbabwe.

questions.question: True or false: A flight from Cape Town to London is a domestic flight.
questions.memo: Cape Town to London crosses international borders and continents, so it is an inter-continental (international) flight, not a domestic one.

questions.question: An _________ flight brings foreign visitors into South Africa from another country.
questions.memo: Inbound flights carry passengers coming INTO the country; outbound flights carry passengers going OUT to other countries.

questions.question: What is a chartered flight?
options: A flight hired for a specific group or purpose, not part of the regular schedule
A flight that always lands at private landing strips
A flight operated only by the national carrier
A flight that carries cargo and never passengers
questions.expected: A flight hired for a specific group or purpose, not part of the regular schedule
questions.memo: A chartered flight is booked (hired) by a person, company or tour group for a specific trip. It does not appear on the airline's normal published timetable.

questions.question: Sort each flight into the correct category.
questions.memo: Domestic = within South Africa; regional = to a nearby Southern African country; inter-continental = to another continent.

questions.question: What is a connecting flight?
options: A flight a passenger changes to in order to reach a final destination
A flight that connects two runways at the same airport
A flight that only carries connecting cables and cargo
The very first flight an airline ever operated
questions.expected: A flight a passenger changes to in order to reach a final destination
questions.memo: A connecting flight is a second (or further) flight a traveller takes after landing, to continue a journey when there is no direct flight to the final destination.

questions.question: True or false: FlySafair is an example of a budget (low-cost) airline operating in South Africa.
questions.memo: Budget airlines such as FlySafair offer lower fares with fewer extras included. SAA is the full-service national carrier.

questions.question: The airport code 'JNB' belongs to which South African airport?
questions.memo: JNB is the code for OR Tambo International (Johannesburg). Cape Town is CPT and King Shaka (Durban) is DUR.

questions.question: A flight that crosses the Atlantic Ocean, such as Johannesburg to New York, is a _________ flight.
questions.memo: A transatlantic flight crosses the Atlantic Ocean. A transcontinental flight crosses a continent, and a regional flight stays within a region.

questions.question: What is the main difference between an international airport and a national (domestic) airport?
options: An international airport handles flights to and from other countries; a national airport mainly handles flights within the country
An international airport is always smaller than a national airport
A national airport may only be used by tourists, not residents
There is no difference; the two terms mean the same thing
questions.expected: An international airport handles flights to and from other countries; a national airport mainly handles flights within the country
questions.memo: International airports have customs and immigration facilities for cross-border flights. National (domestic) airports mainly serve flights inside the country.

questions.question: On an airline timetable, a flight shows 'DEP 14:30'. What does this tell the passenger?
options: The flight is scheduled to depart at 14:30
Boarding closes 14 hours and 30 minutes before take-off
questions.expected: The flight is scheduled to depart at 14:30
questions.memo: On a timetable, 'DEP' means departure time and 'ARR' means arrival time. So DEP 14:30 is the scheduled departure time.

questions.question: Sort each airline into the correct category.
questions.memo: SAA is the national carrier; FlySafair and Lift are budget airlines; Emirates and British Airways are international carriers flying to South Africa.

questions.question: True or false: A private landing strip is a large airport operated by ACSA for scheduled passenger flights.
questions.memo: A private landing strip is a small, privately owned runway (for example on a game farm or lodge) used by private or chartered aircraft, not a large ACSA airport with scheduled flights.

questions.question: A traveller wants the shortest, quickest hop between two nearby cities. Which type of flight is this?
questions.memo: Short-haul flights cover short distances and take little time. Long-haul, transatlantic and transcontinental flights all cover much greater distances.

TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTERMS.A1.title: Airport, aircraft and seating terminology
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTERMS.A1.description: Identify airport areas (landside, terminal, airside), check-in and boarding procedures, baggage allowances, safety steps, aircraft parts (galley, cockpit, cargo hold) and seating configuration (wide-/narrow-body, business/economy, aisle/window/emergency-exit seats).
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTERMS.A1.strand: Term 1 — Transport services in South Africa
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTERMS.A1.caps_topic: Tourism sectors — airport and aircraft terminology
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTERMS.A1.recovery_strategy: Walk through a passenger's journey from kerb to seat, naming each area and step in order.

questions.question: At an airport, what does 'airside' mean?
options: The secure area beyond the security checkpoint, where passengers wait to board
The public area outside, where cars drop off passengers
The roof of the terminal building
questions.expected: The secure area beyond the security checkpoint, where passengers wait to board
questions.memo: Airside is the secure zone past security and passport control, closest to the aircraft. Landside is the public area before security where anyone may go.

questions.question: What is a boarding pass?
options: A document allowing a passenger to board a specific flight, showing seat and gate
A pass that lets visitors enter the cockpit
A receipt for excess baggage charges
A card that opens the hotel room door
questions.expected: A document allowing a passenger to board a specific flight, showing seat and gate
questions.memo: A boarding pass is issued at check-in. It shows the flight number, boarding gate, seat number and boarding time, and is needed to board the aircraft.

questions.question: After landing, passengers collect their checked luggage from the _________ in the baggage claim area.
questions.memo: The carousel is the moving belt in the baggage claim area where checked luggage comes out for passengers to collect.

questions.question: What is the galley on an aircraft?
options: The small kitchen area where cabin crew prepare food and drinks
The area where the pilots fly the plane
The space below the cabin where luggage is stored
questions.expected: The small kitchen area where cabin crew prepare food and drinks
questions.memo: The galley is the aircraft's kitchen, where the cabin crew store and prepare the meals and drinks served on board.

questions.question: True or false: The cockpit is the part of the aircraft where the pilots sit and control the plane.
questions.memo: The cockpit (flight deck) at the front of the aircraft is where the pilots sit and control the flight.

questions.question: What happens at the check-in counter?
options: Passengers register for their flight, hand in checked luggage and receive a boarding pass
Passengers collect their luggage after the flight
Passengers go through the final security search
questions.expected: Passengers register for their flight, hand in checked luggage and receive a boarding pass
questions.memo: At check-in, passengers confirm they are flying, drop off checked bags and receive a boarding pass before going to security.

questions.question: Place these departure steps in the correct order, from first to last.

items.text: Check in and drop off luggage
Pass through the security control point

questions.memo: A departing passenger checks in first, then goes through security, waits at the gate, and finally boards the aircraft.

questions.question: If the cabin loses pressure, oxygen _________ drop down automatically for passengers to use.
questions.memo: Oxygen masks drop from above the seats if cabin pressure is lost, so passengers can breathe normally until the aircraft descends.

questions.question: What is an advantage of choosing an aisle seat?
options: It is easier to get up and move around without disturbing others
It always has the best view of the ground below
It is the only seat with a tray table
It is always in business class
questions.expected: It is easier to get up and move around without disturbing others
questions.memo: An aisle seat is next to the walkway, so it is easy to get up and move around. A window seat gives the best view but is harder to leave during the flight.

questions.question: True or false: Passengers seated in an emergency exit row may be asked to help open the exit in an emergency.
questions.memo: Emergency exit seats usually have extra legroom, but passengers in them must be willing and able to help open the exit and assist in an emergency.

questions.question: Sort each term into whether it is part of the airport or part of the aircraft.
questions.memo: Check-in counters, carousels and gates are found in the airport terminal. The galley, overhead bins and cockpit are parts of the aircraft.

questions.question: Where on an aircraft are checked suitcases stored during the flight?
options: In the cargo hold below the cabin
In the cockpit with the pilots
questions.expected: In the cargo hold below the cabin
questions.memo: Checked luggage travels in the cargo hold beneath the passenger cabin. Small hand luggage goes in the overhead bins inside the cabin.

questions.question: A _________ body aircraft has two aisles and is often used on long-haul flights.
questions.memo: A wide-body aircraft has two aisles and more seats per row, suited to long-haul flights. A narrow-body aircraft has a single aisle and is used on shorter routes.

questions.question: What is the main difference between business class and economy class?
options: Business class offers more space, comfort and service at a higher price than economy class
Economy class is only for business travellers
Business class passengers may fly the aircraft
Economy class always has more legroom than business class
questions.expected: Business class offers more space, comfort and service at a higher price than economy class
questions.memo: Business class costs more and offers wider seats, more legroom and better service. Economy class is the standard, more affordable cabin.

questions.question: True or false: The baggage allowance for a domestic flight is always exactly the same for every passenger and every airline.
questions.memo: Baggage allowances differ between airlines and between fare types (for example budget tickets often allow less). Passengers should always check their airline's allowance.

questions.question: In an airport, what is the 'terminal'?
options: The main building where passengers check in, pass through security and board flights
The runway where aircraft take off and land
questions.expected: The main building where passengers check in, pass through security and board flights
questions.memo: The terminal is the building passengers use — for check-in, security, shops, waiting and boarding. The runway and apron are outside on the airside.

questions.question: Sort each area into whether it is landside or airside at the airport.

items.text: The public arrivals hall where families wait
The kerb where taxis drop off passengers
The duty-free shops past passport control

questions.memo: Landside is before security, open to the public. Airside is after security and passport control, for travelling passengers only.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a speed (self-service) check-in kiosk?
options: To let passengers check themselves in and print a boarding pass quickly, without queueing at a counter
questions.expected: To let passengers check themselves in and print a boarding pass quickly, without queueing at a counter
questions.memo: Self-service kiosks speed up check-in by letting passengers do it themselves and print their own boarding pass, reducing queues at the counters.

questions.question: True or false: Cabin crew give a safety demonstration before take-off so passengers know what to do in an emergency.
questions.memo: Before take-off the crew show the safety procedures — seatbelts, exits, life jackets and oxygen masks — so passengers are prepared for an emergency.

questions.question: What are the overhead storage bins used for?
options: Storing passengers' hand (cabin) luggage during the flight
questions.expected: Storing passengers' hand (cabin) luggage during the flight
questions.memo: Overhead bins above the seats hold passengers' hand luggage. Larger checked bags go in the cargo hold below the cabin.

TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTECH.A1.title: Technology used at airports
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTECH.A1.description: Identify technology that helps travel at airports (baggage wrap, x-ray scanners, biometric and thermal scanners, metal detectors, information display boards, touch-screen systems) and the use of smartphones/PDIs for e-documents and boarding passes ('iTravel').
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTECH.A1.strand: Term 1 — Transport services in South Africa
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTECH.A1.caps_topic: Tourism sectors — technology at airports to facilitate travel
TOUR.G11.T1.AIRTECH.A1.recovery_strategy: Match each device to the problem it solves (security, identification, information, convenience).

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an x-ray security scanner at an airport?
options: To see inside bags and detect prohibited or dangerous items
To cool down the terminal building
questions.expected: To see inside bags and detect prohibited or dangerous items
questions.memo: X-ray scanners let security staff see inside hand luggage without opening it, so they can spot weapons or other banned items.

questions.question: What does a biometric scanner do?
options: Identifies a person using a body feature such as a fingerprint or face
Measures the speed of the aircraft
questions.expected: Identifies a person using a body feature such as a fingerprint or face
questions.memo: Biometric scanners identify travellers by unique body features (fingerprints, faces or eyes), making identity checks faster and more secure.

questions.question: _________ body scanners are used to detect passengers with a raised body temperature, for example during a disease outbreak.
questions.memo: Thermal body scanners detect heat, so they can pick up passengers with a fever — useful for spotting possible illness at the airport.

questions.question: True or false: A metal detector is used to find metal objects a passenger may be carrying.
questions.memo: Walk-through and hand-held metal detectors alert security to metal objects such as keys, coins or possible weapons hidden on a passenger.

questions.question: What information does an airport information display board give passengers?
options: Flight numbers, departure and arrival times, gates and flight status
The recipe served on board the aircraft
questions.expected: Flight numbers, departure and arrival times, gates and flight status
questions.memo: Information display boards show live flight details — times, gates, and whether a flight is boarding, delayed or cancelled — so passengers know where to go.

questions.question: What is the purpose of baggage wrap equipment at an airport?
options: To wrap luggage in protective plastic to guard against damage and tampering
To deliver luggage to the aircraft
questions.expected: To wrap luggage in protective plastic to guard against damage and tampering
questions.memo: Baggage wrapping covers a suitcase in tough plastic to protect it from scratches, dirt, rain and tampering during handling.

questions.question: Many travellers now use their _________ to store electronic tickets and boarding passes for air travel.
questions.memo: Smartphones (a type of PDI) can store e-tickets, boarding passes and travel documents, so travellers no longer always need printed copies.

questions.question: True or false: Touch-screen information systems help passengers find shops, gates and directions inside the terminal.
questions.memo: Touch-screen information kiosks let passengers look up flight information, maps, shops and directions around the airport on their own.

questions.question: What is a benefit of a mobile (electronic) boarding pass on a smartphone?
options: The passenger does not need a printed pass and can board by scanning their phone
It makes the aircraft fly faster
It guarantees a free seat upgrade
It replaces the need for a passport on international flights
questions.expected: The passenger does not need a printed pass and can board by scanning their phone
questions.memo: A mobile boarding pass is stored on the phone and scanned at the gate, saving paper and time. It does not replace a passport for international travel.

questions.question: Sort each airport technology by its main purpose.
questions.memo: Scanners and detectors keep people safe (security); display boards and kiosks share information; baggage wrap and self check-in make travel easier (convenience).

questions.question: During a disease outbreak, which technology would most help screen arriving passengers for fever?
questions.memo: Thermal scanners detect raised body temperature, so they are used to spot passengers who may have a fever during a health emergency.

questions.question: True or false: A biometric scanner identifies people by asking them to type in a password.
questions.memo: Biometric scanners use body features such as fingerprints or faces, not typed passwords, to confirm a person's identity.

questions.question: An electronic _________ pass stored on a phone can replace a printed paper one at the boarding gate.
questions.memo: An electronic boarding pass on a smartphone is scanned at the gate, so the passenger does not need a printed version.

questions.question: What is one general benefit of self-service technology at airports?
options: It speeds up processes and shortens queues for passengers
It removes the need for any airport staff at all
It makes flights cheaper to operate the aircraft
It guarantees flights are never delayed
questions.expected: It speeds up processes and shortens queues for passengers
questions.memo: Self-service technology lets passengers do tasks themselves, which speeds things up and reduces queues, though staff are still needed for help and supervision.

questions.question: What is the difference between a metal detector and an x-ray scanner?
options: A metal detector checks a person for metal; an x-ray scanner sees inside bags
They are exactly the same machine with different names
A metal detector prints boarding passes; an x-ray scanner weighs bags
An x-ray scanner checks people; a metal detector wraps luggage
questions.expected: A metal detector checks a person for metal; an x-ray scanner sees inside bags
questions.memo: Passengers walk through a metal detector, while their bags pass through an x-ray scanner that shows the contents on a screen.

questions.question: Sort each technology by whether it screens for security threats or mainly gives passengers information.
questions.memo: Scanners and detectors check for threats and illness; display boards and kiosks share flight and airport information.

questions.question: True or false: Information display boards are updated to show when a flight is delayed, boarding or cancelled.
questions.memo: Display boards show live, changing flight status so passengers can react to delays, gate changes or cancellations.

questions.question: A PDI used for air travel ('iTravel') most often refers to which of the following?
options: A personal digital device such as a smartphone holding travel documents
questions.expected: A personal digital device such as a smartphone holding travel documents
questions.memo: PDI stands for a personal digital device (like a smartphone). Travellers use it to store electronic tickets, boarding passes and identification — sometimes called 'iTravel'.

questions.question: What is an advantage of biometric scanning at passport control?
options: It confirms identity quickly and is hard to fake
It allows passengers to skip buying a ticket
questions.expected: It confirms identity quickly and is hard to fake
questions.memo: Because biometrics use unique body features, they confirm identity fast and are very difficult to forge, improving both speed and security.

questions.question: X-ray _________ scanners allow staff to check the contents of hand luggage before passengers go airside.
questions.memo: X-ray security scanners are positioned at the security checkpoint so staff can check bag contents before passengers move into the airside area.

TOUR.G11.T1.BUS.A1.title: The tourism bus industry
TOUR.G11.T1.BUS.A1.description: Identify major tourist transporters and the different types of buses (minibuses, coaches, megabuses, sleeper coaches, open-top sightseeing buses) and read the information given on a bus schedule.
TOUR.G11.T1.BUS.A1.strand: Term 1 — Transport services in South Africa
TOUR.G11.T1.BUS.A1.caps_topic: Tourism sectors — the tourism bus industry
TOUR.G11.T1.BUS.A1.recovery_strategy: Match each bus type to a typical trip, then practise reading one schedule row at a time.

questions.question: What is an open-top bus mainly used for?
options: City sightseeing, so tourists can view attractions from an open upper deck
questions.expected: City sightseeing, so tourists can view attractions from an open upper deck
questions.memo: Open-top sightseeing buses (such as City Sightseeing's red buses) let tourists see and photograph city attractions from an open upper deck, often hop-on hop-off.

questions.question: What is the main feature of a sleeper coach?
options: It has beds or bunks so passengers can sleep on long overnight journeys
It has an open roof for sightseeing
It can only carry about eight passengers
It travels only short distances within a city
questions.expected: It has beds or bunks so passengers can sleep on long overnight journeys
questions.memo: A sleeper coach provides beds or bunks so passengers can rest during long overnight trips, arriving more comfortably the next day.

questions.question: A large, comfortable bus used for long-distance group travel is called a _________.
questions.memo: A coach is a large, comfortable bus built for long-distance travel, often with reclining seats, air-conditioning and a toilet.

questions.question: True or false: A minibus carries far fewer passengers than a full-size coach.
questions.memo: A minibus is small and seats roughly 10–22 passengers, while a coach carries many more. Minibuses suit small groups and shuttle services.

questions.question: What is a megabus (double-decker coach)?
options: A very large bus with two levels that can carry many passengers
A small shuttle for a single family
A bus that floats on water
A bus that only carries luggage
questions.expected: A very large bus with two levels that can carry many passengers
questions.memo: A megabus or double-decker coach has two passenger decks, so it carries many more people than a single-deck bus on busy routes.

questions.question: A group of tourists wants to view the main sights of a city while travelling between them. Which bus suits them best?
options: A minibus shuttle to the airport
questions.memo: An open-top sightseeing bus is designed exactly for viewing city attractions, usually with a hop-on hop-off route past the main sights.

questions.question: A bus _________ tells passengers the departure times, routes and stops of the service.
questions.memo: A bus schedule (timetable) lists the routes, stops, departure and arrival times, helping passengers plan their journey.

questions.question: True or false: An open-top sightseeing bus is the best choice for a comfortable overnight journey of 1 000 km.
questions.memo: Open-top buses suit short, slow city sightseeing. For a long overnight trip a sleeper coach or comfortable coach would be far better.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a major long-distance tourist bus transporter in South Africa?
questions.memo: Intercape is a well-known long-distance coach operator. Metrorail and Rovos Rail are trains, and Starlight Cruises operates cruise ships.

questions.question: Match each bus type to the trip it suits best.
questions.memo: Open-top and hop-on hop-off buses are for sightseeing; sleeper coaches suit overnight trips; minibuses handle small-group transfers.

questions.question: Which of the following would you expect to find on a bus schedule?
options: Departure and arrival times, the route and the stops
The colour of every passenger's luggage
The recipe served at the rest stop
questions.expected: Departure and arrival times, the route and the stops
questions.memo: A bus schedule gives travel information: which route the bus follows, where it stops, and the times it departs and arrives.

questions.question: True or false: A sleeper coach is well suited to long overnight journeys between distant cities.
questions.memo: Sleeper coaches have beds or bunks, so passengers can rest overnight on long routes and arrive refreshed.

questions.question: A small bus that seats only about 10 to 22 people, often used as a shuttle, is a _________.
questions.memo: A minibus is the smallest of these, ideal for small groups and short transfers such as airport shuttles.

questions.question: What is an advantage of coach travel for a large tour group?
options: It carries the whole group together comfortably and is cost-effective per person
It is always faster than flying
It can travel on water as well as roads
questions.expected: It carries the whole group together comfortably and is cost-effective per person
questions.memo: Coaches keep a group together, are comfortable for longer trips, and spread the cost across many passengers, making them affordable per person.

questions.question: What is a 'special purpose' bus?
options: A bus adapted for a particular use, such as an open-top bus for sightseeing
Any ordinary bus that runs on a normal route
A bus that may only be driven on weekends
A bus reserved for airport staff
questions.expected: A bus adapted for a particular use, such as an open-top bus for sightseeing
questions.memo: Special purpose buses are built or adapted for a specific use — for example open-top buses for sightseeing — rather than ordinary point-to-point travel.

questions.question: Sort each detail by whether it would appear on a bus schedule.
questions.memo: A schedule lists travel facts — times, routes and stops — not personal details about drivers or passengers.

questions.question: True or false: City Sightseeing's red buses offer a hop-on hop-off service past a city's main attractions.
questions.memo: City Sightseeing operates open-top hop-on hop-off buses that let tourists get on and off at major attractions along a set city route.

questions.question: A travel agent must move a large group comfortably from Johannesburg to Cape Town by road. Which bus is most suitable?
questions.memo: A long-distance coach is comfortable, carries a large group together and is built for the long Johannesburg–Cape Town route.

questions.question: On a bus schedule, which column tells you what time the bus leaves?
questions.memo: The departure column shows when the bus leaves a stop; the arrival column shows when it reaches the destination.

questions.question: A _________ bus has two decks, allowing it to carry many more passengers on a busy route.
questions.memo: A megabus (double-decker) has two passenger levels, so it carries many more people than a single-deck bus.

TOUR.G11.T1.RAIL.A1.title: The tourism train industry and the Gautrain
TOUR.G11.T1.RAIL.A1.description: Tell commuter trains (Metrorail) apart from tourist trains (Shosholoza Meyl), use train terminology (coupé, compartment, dining car, bedding ticket), recognise luxury and scenic trains (Blue Train, Rovos Rail, Premier Classe) and the Gautrain's features, technology and benefits.
TOUR.G11.T1.RAIL.A1.strand: Term 1 — Transport services in South Africa
TOUR.G11.T1.RAIL.A1.caps_topic: Tourism sectors — the tourism train industry and the Gautrain
TOUR.G11.T1.RAIL.A1.recovery_strategy: Contrast a daily commuter trip with a luxury tourist journey, then label train terms with pictures.

questions.question: What kind of train is Metrorail?
options: A commuter train for everyday local travel within cities
A luxury tourist train for sightseeing holidays
A goods-only train that carries no passengers
A high-speed train linking different countries
questions.expected: A commuter train for everyday local travel within cities
questions.memo: Metrorail is a commuter service that carries people on short, everyday trips within and around cities — not a tourist or luxury train.

questions.question: The Blue Train is best described as a:
questions.memo: The Blue Train is one of South Africa's famous luxury tourist trains, offering five-star comfort and scenery on routes such as Pretoria to Cape Town.

questions.question: On a long-distance train, meals are served in the _________ car.
questions.memo: The dining car is the carriage where passengers are served meals during a long train journey.

questions.question: True or false: Shosholoza Meyl is a long-distance passenger train service in South Africa.
questions.memo: Shosholoza Meyl runs long-distance passenger trains between major South African cities, offering an affordable way to travel and see the country.

questions.question: On a train, what is a coupé?
options: A small private compartment, usually for two passengers
The engine that pulls the train
The ticket office on the platform
questions.expected: A small private compartment, usually for two passengers
questions.memo: A coupé is a small private sleeping compartment, typically for two people. A larger compartment sleeps more passengers.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a commuter train and a tourist train?
options: Commuter trains are for everyday short travel; tourist trains are for leisure journeys and sightseeing
Commuter trains are always more luxurious than tourist trains
Tourist trains carry only goods, not people
There is no difference between them
questions.expected: Commuter trains are for everyday short travel; tourist trains are for leisure journeys and sightseeing
questions.memo: Commuter trains (like Metrorail) move people on daily local trips. Tourist trains (like the Blue Train) are about the leisure experience and the scenery along the way.

questions.question: On an overnight train, a _________ ticket lets a passenger hire sheets and blankets for the sleeping berth.
questions.memo: A bedding ticket is bought to hire bedding (sheets, blankets, pillow) for an overnight berth on a long-distance train.

questions.question: True or false: Rovos Rail is one of South Africa's luxury tourist trains.
questions.memo: Rovos Rail is a famous luxury train offering classic, five-star rail journeys and is marketed to tourists seeking a special experience.

questions.question: What is the Gautrain?
options: A modern high-speed rapid-rail service in Gauteng
A cruise ship operating from Durban
questions.expected: A modern high-speed rapid-rail service in Gauteng
questions.memo: The Gautrain is a fast, modern rapid-rail system in Gauteng, linking Johannesburg, Pretoria, Sandton and OR Tambo International Airport.

questions.question: Sort each train into the correct category.
questions.memo: Metrorail and the Gautrain move people on everyday journeys. The Blue Train, Rovos Rail, Premier Classe and Shongololo Express are luxury tourist trains.

questions.question: Which is an example of Gautrain technology that makes travel easier?
options: A reloadable smartcard for electronic ticketing and boarding
A dining car serving five-course meals
questions.expected: A reloadable smartcard for electronic ticketing and boarding
questions.memo: The Gautrain uses a reloadable Gautrain card for electronic ticketing and tap-in boarding, with electronic arrival and departure announcements.

questions.question: True or false: The Gautrain is linked to a bus service and offers parking at stations to make travel more convenient.
questions.memo: Gautrain feeder buses and station parking help passengers reach and leave the stations easily, encouraging more people to use the train.

questions.question: _________ Rail is a well-known South African luxury train offering classic, vintage-style journeys.
questions.memo: Rovos Rail is famous for its restored vintage carriages and luxury, slow-travel tourist journeys.

questions.question: What is one benefit of the Gautrain for tourism in Gauteng?
options: It gives tourists a fast, safe link between the airport and city centres, reducing road traffic
It replaces the need for any hotels in the province
It only carries cargo, freeing up the roads
It removes the need for tourists to carry passports
questions.expected: It gives tourists a fast, safe link between the airport and city centres, reducing road traffic
questions.memo: The Gautrain offers tourists a quick, reliable, safe link from OR Tambo to business and city areas, easing road congestion and supporting tourism.

questions.question: What information would you expect to find on a train schedule?
options: Departure and arrival times, stations and the class of travel
The names of all the passengers
questions.expected: Departure and arrival times, stations and the class of travel
questions.memo: A train schedule lists the route stations, the departure and arrival times and the classes of travel available.

questions.question: Match each train term to its meaning.
questions.memo: The dining car serves meals; a coupé is a small private compartment; a bedding ticket lets you hire bedding for the night.

questions.question: True or false: Premier Classe is a more comfortable, premium long-distance train service.
questions.memo: Premier Classe offers a premium, more comfortable long-distance rail experience with better service than standard economy travel.

questions.question: What is the main appeal of a scenic or heritage tourist train?
options: The journey itself — beautiful scenery or a nostalgic, historic experience
Getting to work as cheaply as possible
Carrying heavy freight across the country
Reaching the destination as fast as possible
questions.expected: The journey itself — beautiful scenery or a nostalgic, historic experience
questions.memo: Scenic and heritage trains are about enjoying the ride — the views and the sense of history — rather than simply getting somewhere quickly.

questions.question: Which of these is on a Gautrain route?
questions.memo: The Gautrain links OR Tambo International Airport with Sandton, Johannesburg and Pretoria — all within Gauteng.

questions.question: _________ trains, such as Metrorail, carry large numbers of people on short daily trips in and around cities.
questions.memo: Commuter trains move many people on short, regular journeys for work and daily life, unlike luxury or scenic tourist trains.

TOUR.G11.T1.CRUISE.A1.title: The luxury cruise liner industry
TOUR.G11.T1.CRUISE.A1.description: Use cruise concepts (port, cruise terminal, state rooms, cabins, suites, decks), describe the facilities and entertainment on board, and read the information given on a cruise package.
TOUR.G11.T1.CRUISE.A1.strand: Term 1 — Transport services in South Africa
TOUR.G11.T1.CRUISE.A1.caps_topic: Tourism sectors — the luxury cruise liner industry
TOUR.G11.T1.CRUISE.A1.recovery_strategy: Tour a cruise ship layout from port to cabin, naming each concept, then read one package detail at a time.

questions.question: In the cruise industry, what is a port?
options: A harbour where the ship docks to take on or drop off passengers
A type of cabin on the ship
questions.expected: A harbour where the ship docks to take on or drop off passengers
questions.memo: A port is a harbour where the cruise ship stops so passengers can board, leave, or go ashore to explore a destination.

questions.question: What is a cabin on a cruise ship?
options: The room where the ship is steered
questions.memo: A cabin is the private bedroom where passengers sleep on board. Larger, more luxurious versions are called suites.

questions.question: On a ship, each level or floor is called a _________.
questions.memo: The decks are the floors of a ship. Different decks hold cabins, restaurants, pools and entertainment areas.

questions.question: True or false: A suite is a larger and more luxurious room than a standard cabin.
questions.memo: A suite offers more space, comfort and often a private balcony, making it more luxurious (and more expensive) than a standard cabin.

questions.question: What is a cruise terminal used for?
options: It is the building where passengers check in, board and disembark the ship
It is the engine room of the ship
It is the top deck used for sunbathing
questions.expected: It is the building where passengers check in, board and disembark the ship
questions.memo: A cruise terminal is the building at the port where passengers are processed to board the ship and where they leave it at the end of the cruise.

questions.question: What is a 'state room' on a cruise ship?
options: A private passenger room or cabin on board
A room only the government may use
The room where life jackets are stored
questions.expected: A private passenger room or cabin on board
questions.memo: State room is another name for a passenger's private cabin on board a cruise ship.

questions.question: Passengers check in and board the ship at the cruise _________.
questions.memo: The cruise terminal is where passengers are checked in and board the ship before the voyage begins.

questions.question: True or false: A cruise package usually includes accommodation, meals and entertainment on board in one price.
questions.memo: Cruises are often largely all-inclusive: the price typically covers the cabin, most meals and the onboard entertainment, though some extras cost more.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a facility found on a large cruise ship?
questions.memo: Large cruise ships offer facilities such as swimming pools, gyms, shops, theatres and restaurants for passengers to use on board.

questions.question: Sort each item by whether it is found on a cruise ship.

buckets.label: Not part of a cruise ship

questions.memo: Cabins, suites, sun decks and theatres are part of a cruise ship. A cockpit belongs to an aircraft and a dining car to a train.

questions.question: Which of these is a form of entertainment offered on board a cruise ship?
options: Live shows in the onboard theatre
A car-rental desk in the cabin
questions.expected: Live shows in the onboard theatre
questions.memo: Cruise ships offer entertainment such as live theatre shows, music, casinos, films and activities to keep passengers busy at sea.

questions.question: True or false: The decks on a cruise ship are numbered floors where cabins and facilities are arranged.
questions.memo: Decks are the ship's floors, usually numbered, and the cabins, restaurants and other facilities are spread across them.

questions.question: A cruise ship docks at a _________ so that passengers can go ashore to explore a destination.
questions.memo: When a ship stops at a port, passengers can disembark to sightsee or shop before returning to continue the cruise.

questions.question: Which information would you expect to find on a cruise package?
options: The route, the ports visited, the cabin type and the price
The home addresses of all the crew
The colour of every cabin door
questions.expected: The route, the ports visited, the cabin type and the price
questions.memo: A cruise package describes the route (itinerary), the ports the ship visits, the cabin or suite type, what is included and the price.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a cabin and a suite?
options: A suite is larger and more luxurious; a standard cabin is smaller and cheaper
A cabin is on land; a suite is on the ship
A suite has no bed; a cabin does
There is no difference between them
questions.expected: A suite is larger and more luxurious; a standard cabin is smaller and cheaper
questions.memo: Both are passenger rooms, but a suite offers more space and luxury (often a balcony) at a higher price than a standard cabin.

questions.question: Match each cruise term to its meaning.

items.text: Harbour stop where passengers go ashore

questions.memo: A port is the harbour stop, a deck is a floor of the ship, and a suite is a large luxury cabin.

questions.question: True or false: Starlight Cruises is an operator that markets cruise holidays to South African tourists.
questions.memo: Starlight Cruises markets cruise holidays departing from South African ports such as Durban and Cape Town to local tourists.

questions.question: What is an advantage of a cruise holiday for a tourist?
options: You can visit several destinations while unpacking only once, with meals and entertainment included
You must arrange separate accommodation in every port
You can never leave the ship
It is the fastest way to cross between continents
questions.expected: You can visit several destinations while unpacking only once, with meals and entertainment included
questions.memo: A cruise lets travellers see several ports on one trip while staying in the same cabin, with food and entertainment usually included in the price.

questions.question: What is the difference between an inside cabin and an ocean-view cabin?
options: An inside cabin has no window; an ocean-view cabin has a window or porthole facing the sea
An inside cabin is on land; an ocean-view cabin is on the ship
An ocean-view cabin has no bed
There is no difference in price between them
questions.expected: An inside cabin has no window; an ocean-view cabin has a window or porthole facing the sea
questions.memo: Inside cabins have no outside window and are usually cheaper. Ocean-view cabins have a window or porthole, so they cost more.

questions.question: A luxury _________ is a larger cabin with extra space and comfort, often including a private balcony.
questions.memo: A suite is the most spacious and luxurious type of passenger room on a cruise ship, often with a balcony and sitting area.

TOUR.G11.T1.CARRENTAL.A1.title: Car rental: conditions, packages and costs
TOUR.G11.T1.CARRENTAL.A1.description: Explain the conditions for renting a vehicle (age, licence, creditworthiness, contract), the rental packages and insurances (CDW, SCDW, TLW, PAI), and the additional, optional and incidental costs that affect a car-rental quotation.
TOUR.G11.T1.CARRENTAL.A1.strand: Term 1 — Transport services in South Africa
TOUR.G11.T1.CARRENTAL.A1.recovery_strategy: Group the charges into compulsory, optional and incidental, then walk through one quotation step by step.

questions.question: Which of these is a condition a customer must usually meet to rent a vehicle?
options: Own a house in South Africa
Be a member of a travel club
questions.memo: To rent a car a customer must have a valid driver's licence, meet a minimum age, be creditworthy (usually a credit card) and sign the rental contract.

questions.question: What does Collision Damage Waiver (CDW) cover?
options: It limits the renter's liability for damage to the rental vehicle in an accident
It pays the renter's traffic fines
It covers theft of the renter's personal luggage
It pays for the fuel used during the rental
questions.expected: It limits the renter's liability for damage to the rental vehicle in an accident
questions.memo: CDW reduces how much the renter must pay for damage to the rental car if there is a collision. It does not cover fines, fuel or personal items.

questions.question: PAI stands for Personal _________ Insurance, which covers injury to the driver and passengers.
questions.memo: PAI is Personal Accident Insurance, covering medical costs if the driver or passengers are injured in an accident.

questions.question: True or false: A customer must usually meet a minimum age to rent a vehicle.
questions.memo: Car-rental companies set a minimum age (often 21–23) because younger drivers are seen as higher risk. Age is one of the standard rental conditions.

questions.question: What does Theft Loss Waiver (TLW) cover?
options: It limits the renter's liability if the rental vehicle is stolen
It pays for any speeding fines
It covers damage from a collision
questions.expected: It limits the renter's liability if the rental vehicle is stolen
questions.memo: TLW reduces what the renter must pay if the rental car is stolen. CDW, by contrast, covers collision damage.

questions.question: Which of these is an OPTIONAL extra charge, chosen only if the customer wants it?
questions.memo: Adding a second driver is optional and only charged if requested. The daily rate and tourism levy are part of the standard cost.

questions.question: A cross-_________ fee is charged when a renter takes the vehicle into another country.
questions.memo: A cross-border fee applies when the rental car is driven into a neighbouring country, covering extra paperwork and permits.

questions.question: True or false: A traffic fine received during the rental is an incidental cost the renter must pay.
questions.memo: Incidental costs arise from how the car is used — such as traffic fines or an admin fee after an accident — and the renter is responsible for them.

questions.question: How does Super Collision Damage Waiver (SCDW) differ from ordinary CDW?
options: SCDW reduces the renter's excess (the amount they still pay) even further than CDW
SCDW covers traffic fines while CDW does not
SCDW is always free of charge
SCDW covers theft while CDW covers fuel
questions.expected: SCDW reduces the renter's excess (the amount they still pay) even further than CDW
questions.memo: SCDW (Super CDW) lowers the excess the renter must still pay after damage, giving more protection than standard CDW, for a higher fee.

questions.question: Sort each car-rental cost into the correct type.
questions.memo: Standard/additional charges (levy, surcharge) are part of the quote; optional extras (extra driver, GPS) are chosen; incidental costs (fines, accident admin) depend on what happens during the rental.

questions.question: In car rental, what is the 'excess'?
options: The amount the renter must still pay towards damage or theft, even with a waiver
Extra fuel left in the tank at the end
The number of free kilometres included
The deposit returned at the end of the rental
questions.expected: The amount the renter must still pay towards damage or theft, even with a waiver
questions.memo: The excess is the portion of a claim the renter is responsible for. Buying SCDW/STLW lowers this excess.

questions.question: True or false: A renter must sign a rental contract before driving away with the vehicle.
questions.memo: Signing the rental contract is a condition of hiring a car; it sets out the terms, costs and the renter's responsibilities.

questions.question: Rental companies require customers to be _________worthy, usually shown by holding a valid credit card.
questions.memo: Being creditworthy (normally proven with a credit card) reassures the company that the renter can cover deposits, damage or extra charges.

questions.question: Which payment method is most commonly required to secure a car rental and its deposit?
questions.memo: A credit card is usually needed so the company can hold a deposit and recover any damage, fines or extra costs after the rental.

questions.question: Place the car-rental steps in the correct order, from first to last.

items.text: Choose a vehicle and rental package
Present your driver's licence and credit card
Return the vehicle and settle any extra charges

questions.memo: First choose the package, then present your documents, sign the contract, collect the car, and finally return it and pay any extras.

questions.question: Match each car-rental insurance to what it mainly covers.
questions.memo: CDW/SCDW cover damage to the car; TLW/STLW cover theft of the car; PAI covers injury to the driver and passengers.

questions.question: The tourism levy added to a car-rental quotation is an example of:
options: An additional charge included in the cost of the rental
An optional extra the customer chooses
questions.expected: An additional charge included in the cost of the rental
questions.memo: The tourism levy is an additional charge that forms part of the standard rental cost, not an optional extra or an insurance.

questions.question: Option A costs R450 per day with 200 free km. Option B costs R400 per day plus R1,50 per km. For one day driving 100 km, which is cheaper?
options: Option A at R450 (Option B works out to R550)
questions.expected: Option A at R450 (Option B works out to R550)
questions.memo: Option A is a flat R450 (100 km is within the 200 free km). Option B = R400 + (100 × R1,50) = R400 + R150 = R550. So Option A is cheaper.

questions.question: True or false: Personal Accident Insurance (PAI) covers injuries to the driver and passengers.
questions.memo: PAI covers medical costs for injuries to the driver and passengers in an accident, unlike CDW (vehicle damage) or TLW (theft).

questions.question: After an accident, the rental company may charge the renter an admin _________ to process the paperwork.
questions.memo: An administration fee is an incidental cost charged to cover the paperwork and processing after an accident or fine.

TOUR.G11.T2.DTGS.A1.title: The Domestic Tourism Growth Strategy
TOUR.G11.T2.DTGS.A1.description: Explain the purpose of the Domestic Tourism Growth Strategy (DTGS), its objectives (sustainable growth, transformation, empowerment and jobs) and the ways it grows domestic tourism (more trips, longer stays, reducing seasonality, better geographic spread, using events, improving safety).
TOUR.G11.T2.DTGS.A1.strand: Term 2 — Domestic growth, culture and foreign exchange
TOUR.G11.T2.DTGS.A1.caps_topic: Domestic, regional and international tourism — the Domestic Tourism Growth Strategy
TOUR.G11.T2.DTGS.A1.recovery_strategy: Separate the 'why' (objectives) from the 'how' (methods), using one local example for each.

questions.question: What is the main aim of the Domestic Tourism Growth Strategy (DTGS)?
options: To grow tourism by getting more South Africans to travel within their own country
To attract more overseas visitors to South Africa
To stop South Africans from travelling abroad
To increase the number of international flights only
questions.expected: To grow tourism by getting more South Africans to travel within their own country
questions.memo: The DTGS focuses on domestic tourism — encouraging South Africans to explore and travel within South Africa, which spreads the benefits of tourism more widely.

questions.question: Which of these is an objective of the DTGS?
options: Reducing the number of national parks
Raising the cost of domestic travel
questions.memo: The DTGS objectives include sustainable growth, transforming the sector, and empowering people while creating jobs.

questions.question: Encouraging people to travel all year round, not only in peak periods, is a way of reducing _________.
questions.memo: Reducing seasonality means spreading travel across the whole year so the industry is not overloaded in holidays and quiet the rest of the time.

questions.question: True or false: The Domestic Tourism Growth Strategy is mainly about attracting overseas tourists to South Africa.
questions.memo: The DTGS is about domestic tourism — South Africans travelling within South Africa — not about attracting foreign visitors.

questions.question: What does 'improving the geographic spread of tourism' mean?
options: Encouraging more trips to less popular provinces, not only the well-known spots
Building tourism only in the busiest provinces
Spreading tourists evenly across other countries
Reducing the total number of trips taken
questions.expected: Encouraging more trips to less popular provinces, not only the well-known spots
questions.memo: Improving geographic spread means getting tourists to visit a wider range of places, so quieter provinces also benefit from tourism income and jobs.

questions.question: Which is an example of increasing tourism expenditure?
options: Encouraging travellers to stay longer and take more trips
Reducing the number of provinces tourists may visit
questions.expected: Encouraging travellers to stay longer and take more trips
questions.memo: Increasing expenditure means getting people to spend more — by taking more trips, staying longer and spending more on each trip.

questions.question: The DTGS wants to increase volumes by getting more _________ Africans to travel within the country.
questions.memo: Increasing volumes means getting a larger number of South Africans to travel domestically, growing the overall size of domestic tourism.

questions.question: True or false: Using events such as festivals to encourage year-round travel is one of the DTGS methods.
questions.memo: Events and festivals draw visitors throughout the year, helping reduce seasonality and spread tourism to different areas.

questions.question: Why does the DTGS include improving safety and reducing crime?
options: Travellers are more likely to take trips when they feel safe
Crime has no effect on whether people travel
It is only meant to reduce the cost of flights
questions.expected: Travellers are more likely to take trips when they feel safe
questions.memo: Safety influences travel decisions. When people feel safe, more of them are willing to travel, which supports the growth of domestic tourism.

questions.question: Sort each statement into whether it is a DTGS objective (a goal) or a method (a way to reach it).

items.text: Sustainable growth of the tourism sector
Promoting trips to less popular provinces
Using events to draw year-round visitors

questions.memo: Objectives are the goals (growth, transformation, jobs). Methods are the actions used to reach them (reducing seasonality, spreading trips, using events).

questions.question: Who is a domestic tourist?
options: A South African travelling within South Africa
A foreign visitor arriving in South Africa
questions.expected: A South African travelling within South Africa
questions.memo: Domestic tourists travel within their own country. The DTGS aims to grow exactly this kind of travel.

questions.question: True or false: Encouraging trips outside the busy school-holiday periods helps reduce seasonality.
questions.memo: Spreading travel beyond peak holidays keeps the industry busier all year, which is the goal of reducing seasonality.

questions.question: Tourism sector _________ aims to make the industry fairer and more inclusive for all South Africans.
questions.memo: Transformation means changing the industry so more South Africans, especially those previously excluded, can take part and benefit.

questions.question: What is a benefit of spreading tourism to less popular provinces?
options: More areas earn tourism income and create jobs, not only the busy hotspots
It reduces the total amount of money spent on tourism
It forces all tourists into one province
It closes attractions in popular areas
questions.expected: More areas earn tourism income and create jobs, not only the busy hotspots
questions.memo: When tourism reaches quieter provinces, the income, jobs and development are shared more widely across the country.

questions.question: What does 'increasing volumes' mean in the DTGS?
options: Getting a larger number of South Africans to travel domestically
Turning up the volume of music at events
questions.expected: Getting a larger number of South Africans to travel domestically
questions.memo: Increasing volumes is about growing the number of domestic travellers — more people taking trips within South Africa.

questions.question: Sort each action under the DTGS aim it best supports.

items.text: Encourage longer stays and more trips
Get travellers to spend more per trip
Use winter events to draw visitors

questions.memo: Longer stays and higher spend raise expenditure; off-peak travel and events reduce seasonality; marketing quieter areas improves geographic spread.

questions.question: True or false: One DTGS objective is the sustainable growth and development of the tourism sector.
questions.memo: Sustainable tourism sector growth and development is a core objective, so the industry grows in a lasting, responsible way.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of reducing seasonality?
options: Running a popular festival in the off-peak winter months
Closing all attractions except in December
questions.expected: Running a popular festival in the off-peak winter months
questions.memo: Holding events in quieter months attracts visitors year-round, smoothing out the peaks and troughs of seasonal travel.

questions.question: How does empowerment and job creation in tourism benefit communities?
options: It gives people skills, work and income, improving their lives
It only benefits large overseas companies
It removes jobs from local areas
It has no effect on local people
questions.expected: It gives people skills, work and income, improving their lives
questions.memo: By creating jobs and developing skills, tourism empowers local people with income and opportunities, supporting whole communities.

questions.question: A growth _________ is a plan setting out how to increase tourism over time.
questions.memo: A growth strategy is a planned approach with clear goals and methods for increasing tourism — exactly what the DTGS sets out.

TOUR.G11.T2.SEGMENTS.A1.title: The seven domestic travel market segments
TOUR.G11.T2.SEGMENTS.A1.description: Explain why domestic tourists are grouped into segments and recognise the seven DTGS segments (e.g. young and upcoming, striving families, golden active couples), matching each segment profile to the holiday products it prefers.
TOUR.G11.T2.SEGMENTS.A1.strand: Term 2 — Domestic growth, culture and foreign exchange
TOUR.G11.T2.SEGMENTS.A1.caps_topic: Domestic, regional and international tourism — the seven domestic travel market segments
TOUR.G11.T2.SEGMENTS.A1.recovery_strategy: Describe each segment as a real person, then match that person to one suitable product at a time.

questions.question: What is market segmentation in tourism?
options: Dividing tourists into groups that share similar needs and travel behaviour
Selling holidays at the same price to everyone
Closing the market to new tourists
Offering only one type of holiday to all travellers
questions.expected: Dividing tourists into groups that share similar needs and travel behaviour
questions.memo: Segmentation splits the broad market into smaller groups (segments) of people with similar needs, so each group can be marketed to more effectively.

questions.question: Why do marketers divide domestic tourists into segments?
options: So they can match the right products and messages to each group
So they can charge everyone exactly the same
So they can stop people from travelling
So they can ignore what travellers actually want
questions.expected: So they can match the right products and messages to each group
questions.memo: Segmentation lets marketers offer suitable products and target their messages to each group's needs, which improves results.

questions.question: A segment _________ describes the typical features of a group, such as their age, income and the holidays they like.
questions.memo: A segment profile is a description of a group's typical characteristics — who they are, how they travel and what they prefer.

questions.question: True or false: All domestic tourists want exactly the same kind of holiday.
questions.memo: Different groups want different things — that is why the market is split into segments, each with its own preferred products.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the seven DTGS domestic travel market segments?
questions.memo: Golden active couples (older, active travellers) are one of the seven DTGS segments. The others listed are not domestic segments.

questions.question: Which segment is described as older but still active, with the time and money to travel?
questions.memo: Golden active couples are older couples who are still active and able to spend on travel, so they suit a range of leisure products.

questions.question: _________ segments are newer, growing groups that are starting to travel more.
questions.memo: Emerging segments are growing groups whose travel is increasing. Established segments already travel regularly, and untapped segments hardly travel yet.

questions.question: True or false: 'Striving families' is one of the seven DTGS domestic travel market segments.
questions.memo: Striving families are indeed one of the seven segments, alongside groups such as young and upcoming and golden active couples.

questions.question: What does an 'established' segment mean?
options: A group that already travels regularly
A group that has never travelled
A group that only travels overseas
A group that is shrinking and disappearing
questions.expected: A group that already travels regularly
questions.memo: Established segments are groups that are already active travellers. Emerging segments are growing, and untapped segments rarely travel yet.

questions.question: Match each holiday product to the kind of experience it offers.

items.text: A relaxing beach holiday by the sea
A game-viewing stay in a wildlife reserve
A short trip to enjoy a city's shops and nightlife
Surfing and sunbathing on the coast
A safari lodge in the bushveld
A weekend exploring museums and restaurants downtown

questions.memo: Coastal getaways are beach holidays; bush retreats are wildlife stays; city breaks are short urban trips.

questions.question: What is a 'city break' product?
options: A short holiday spent enjoying a city's attractions
A beach holiday on the coast
questions.expected: A short holiday spent enjoying a city's attractions
questions.memo: A city break is a short trip to enjoy a city — its shops, restaurants, nightlife and attractions.

questions.question: True or false: Untapped segments are groups that do not yet travel much but could be encouraged to.
questions.memo: Untapped segments hardly travel at present, but they offer growth potential if they can be encouraged to start.

questions.question: 'Golden active _________' are older travellers who are still fit and enjoy getting out and about.
questions.memo: The 'golden active couples' segment is made up of older couples who remain active and like to travel.

questions.question: Which product would best suit young travellers looking for excitement and a lively atmosphere?
options: Event wonders, such as a music festival
A still, silent retreat with no activities
questions.expected: Event wonders, such as a music festival
questions.memo: Event wonders are holidays built around events like festivals or sport, which appeal to young, energetic travellers seeking excitement.

questions.question: Which of these is included in segment statistics?
options: The size of the segment, when they travel and how long they stay
The names of every person in the segment
The colour of each traveller's car
The pilot of every flight they take
questions.expected: The size of the segment, when they travel and how long they stay
questions.memo: Segment statistics describe a group's size, when they travel, how long they stay, who they travel with and the transport they use.

questions.question: Sort each group by how much it currently travels.

items.text: A group that already takes several trips a year
A group that is starting to travel more each year
A group that rarely travels but could be encouraged to
A newly growing group of travellers

questions.memo: Established segments travel regularly, emerging segments are increasing their travel, and untapped segments barely travel yet.

questions.question: True or false: A 'bush retreat' product offers wildlife and game-viewing in a reserve.
questions.memo: Bush retreats are holidays in the bushveld or game reserves, focused on wildlife and nature.

questions.question: What does a 'coastal getaway' product offer?
options: A holiday at the sea, with beaches and coastal activities
A wildlife safari in the bush
A shopping trip in the city centre
questions.expected: A holiday at the sea, with beaches and coastal activities
questions.memo: Coastal getaways are seaside holidays focused on beaches, swimming and coastal activities.

questions.question: What is the benefit of matching a segment to the right product?
options: The marketing is more effective and more travellers are likely to buy
It guarantees no one will ever travel
It makes all products cost the same
It removes the need to advertise at all
questions.expected: The marketing is more effective and more travellers are likely to buy
questions.memo: Offering each segment the product it actually wants makes marketing more effective and increases the chance of a sale.

questions.question: _________ discoveries are holidays focused on experiencing local culture and heritage.
questions.memo: Cultural discoveries are trips built around exploring local culture, traditions and heritage.

TOUR.G11.T2.CULTURE.A1.title: South African cultural uniqueness
TOUR.G11.T2.CULTURE.A1.description: Identify the cultural features that attract tourists to South Africa (folklore, dress, cuisine, gumboot dancing, Ndebele art, Zulu dance, sangomas and traditional healing, rickshaws, San heritage, art festivals) and explain how cultural diversity promotes inbound and domestic tourism.
TOUR.G11.T2.CULTURE.A1.strand: Term 2 — Domestic growth, culture and foreign exchange
TOUR.G11.T2.CULTURE.A1.caps_topic: Culture and heritage — South African cultural uniqueness
TOUR.G11.T2.CULTURE.A1.recovery_strategy: Link each cultural feature to the experience a tourist would have, then test one example at a time.

questions.question: What is gumboot dancing?
options: A rhythmic dance that grew out of South Africa's gold-mining culture
questions.expected: A rhythmic dance that grew out of South Africa's gold-mining culture
questions.memo: Gumboot dancing developed among mineworkers, who used their rubber boots to make rhythms. It is now a popular performance that attracts tourists.

questions.question: Ndebele culture is especially well known to tourists for which art form?
options: Bold, colourful geometric patterns painted on houses and made into beadwork
questions.expected: Bold, colourful geometric patterns painted on houses and made into beadwork
questions.memo: Ndebele art is famous for bright, geometric patterns on house walls and in beadwork, and is a strong draw for cultural tourists.

questions.question: A traditional healer in many South African cultures is called a _________.
questions.memo: A sangoma is a traditional healer who uses traditional medicine and spiritual practices. This heritage interests many cultural tourists.

questions.question: True or false: South Africa's cultural diversity can attract tourists from around the world.
questions.memo: South Africa's many cultures, languages and traditions are a unique attraction that draws both international and domestic tourists.

questions.question: Colourful hand-pulled rickshaws drawn by men in beaded Zulu costume are a well-known cultural sight in which city?
questions.memo: Durban's beachfront is famous for its decorated rickshaws pulled by men in traditional Zulu attire — a popular cultural attraction.

questions.question: What mainly attracts a cultural tourist to South Africa?
options: The chance to experience local customs, food, dance, dress and traditions
Only the chance to shop for foreign brands
The lowest possible prices on flights
questions.expected: The chance to experience local customs, food, dance, dress and traditions
questions.memo: Cultural tourists travel to experience how people live — their food, music, dance, dress and traditions — which South Africa offers in great variety.

questions.question: Traditional _________ involves healing with natural remedies and is part of South Africa's cultural heritage.
questions.memo: Traditional medicine uses natural and herbal remedies, often practised by healers such as sangomas, and forms part of cultural heritage.

questions.question: True or false: The San are one of the oldest cultural groups in Southern Africa, known for their rock art.
questions.memo: The San are among the region's oldest peoples, famous for their ancient rock art, which is an important cultural and heritage attraction.

questions.question: What is folklore?
options: The traditional stories, beliefs and customs passed down within a culture
questions.expected: The traditional stories, beliefs and customs passed down within a culture
questions.memo: Folklore is the traditional stories, legends, beliefs and customs handed down through the generations, which give a culture its identity.

questions.question: Sort each cultural feature into the correct category.
questions.memo: Gumboot and Zulu dancing are performances; Ndebele painting and San rock art are art forms; sangomas and traditional medicine are healing and belief practices.

questions.question: Zulu dancing performed in traditional attire is an example of:
options: A cultural performance that attracts tourists
questions.expected: A cultural performance that attracts tourists
questions.memo: Traditional Zulu dancing is a vibrant cultural performance that draws visitors wanting to experience South African heritage.

questions.question: True or false: Local cuisine has nothing to do with cultural tourism.
questions.memo: Food is a major part of culture. Tasting traditional dishes is one of the main reasons cultural tourists travel.

questions.question: _________ art, linked to kwaito music, grew out of South Africa's townships.
questions.memo: Township art and music, including kwaito, are a modern part of South African culture that interests many visitors.

questions.question: How does South Africa's cultural uniqueness promote inbound tourism?
options: Foreign visitors travel here to experience cultures they cannot find at home
It makes flights to South Africa cheaper
It has no effect on foreign visitors
questions.expected: Foreign visitors travel here to experience cultures they cannot find at home
questions.memo: Unique cultures give foreign tourists a reason to choose South Africa, drawing inbound visitors who want an authentic, different experience.

questions.question: What is one benefit of an art or cultural festival for tourism?
options: It attracts visitors and showcases local culture and talent
It keeps tourists away from the area
It replaces the need for any accommodation
It stops local artists from performing
questions.expected: It attracts visitors and showcases local culture and talent
questions.memo: Festivals draw crowds, celebrate local culture and creativity, and bring income to the host area — a strong cultural tourism draw.

questions.question: Sort each item by whether it is a South African cultural attraction.
questions.memo: Ndebele beadwork, gumboot dancing and Zulu rickshaws are cultural attractions. An x-ray scanner and a rental fee are not.

questions.question: True or false: Small chiefdoms with traditional leaders form part of South Africa's cultural heritage.
questions.memo: Traditional leadership and small chiefdoms are part of the country's living cultural heritage and can interest cultural tourists.

questions.question: Why is South Africa's cultural diversity considered a tourism strength?
options: Many different cultures in one country give tourists a rich variety of experiences
It makes the country harder to visit
It means there is only one thing to see
It reduces the number of attractions available
questions.expected: Many different cultures in one country give tourists a rich variety of experiences
questions.memo: Having many cultures together means tourists can experience a wide variety of traditions, food, music and art in a single destination.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of traditional cultural dress used to attract tourists?
options: Beaded Zulu attire worn during traditional dancing
questions.expected: Beaded Zulu attire worn during traditional dancing
questions.memo: Traditional dress, such as beaded Zulu attire, is part of cultural performances that showcase heritage to tourists.

questions.question: _________ dancing developed from the culture of South Africa's gold mines.
questions.memo: Gumboot dancing began among mineworkers who used their boots to communicate and make rhythms, and is now a celebrated cultural performance.

TOUR.G11.T2.HERITAGE.A1.title: South African heritage bodies
TOUR.G11.T2.HERITAGE.A1.description: Describe the South African Heritage Resources Agency (SAHRA) and provincial heritage agencies, their functions, and the protection rules and permits for heritage items (structures older than 60 years, archaeological and palaeontological sites, meteorites, shipwrecks, graves).
TOUR.G11.T2.HERITAGE.A1.strand: Term 2 — Domestic growth, culture and foreign exchange
TOUR.G11.T2.HERITAGE.A1.caps_topic: Culture and heritage — South African heritage bodies
TOUR.G11.T2.HERITAGE.A1.recovery_strategy: Connect SAHRA's job to protecting specific items, then decide 'protected or not' for one example at a time.

questions.question: What is the main job of the South African Heritage Resources Agency (SAHRA)?
options: To protect and manage South Africa's heritage resources
To sell heritage sites to private owners
To set the prices of air tickets
questions.expected: To protect and manage South Africa's heritage resources
questions.memo: SAHRA is the national body responsible for identifying, protecting and managing South Africa's heritage resources so they are preserved for the future.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation SAHRA stand for?
options: South African Hotel and Restaurant Association
Southern Airports and Harbours Regulatory Authority
questions.memo: SAHRA is the South African Heritage Resources Agency, the national heritage protection body.

questions.question: In South Africa, structures older than _________ years are protected and may not be altered or demolished without a permit.
questions.memo: Structures older than 60 years are protected, so a permit is needed before changing or demolishing them.

questions.question: True or false: You need a special permit before disturbing a shipwreck or a grave.
questions.memo: Shipwrecks, graves and burial grounds are protected heritage, so a permit is required before they may be disturbed.

questions.question: Which of these is protected as a heritage resource?
options: An archaeological site with ancient artefacts
A current model of rental car
questions.expected: An archaeological site with ancient artefacts
questions.memo: Archaeological sites and their materials are protected heritage. New, ordinary buildings and vehicles are not.

questions.question: What is the role of provincial heritage agencies?
options: To protect and manage heritage resources at provincial level
questions.expected: To protect and manage heritage resources at provincial level
questions.memo: Provincial heritage agencies look after heritage within their province, working alongside the national body, SAHRA.

questions.question: Fossils found at _________ sites are protected and may not be removed without permission.
questions.memo: Palaeontological sites contain fossils, which are protected heritage materials that may not be removed without a permit.

questions.question: True or false: Anyone may freely remove an old gravestone from a protected burial ground.
questions.memo: Graves and burial grounds are protected. Removing or disturbing them without a permit is illegal.

questions.question: Why is it important to protect heritage resources?
options: To preserve them for future generations and keep them as attractions
To make sure tourists can never see them
So they can be sold off quickly
Because they have no value at all
