questions.question: Which of these careers is in the hospitality sector?
questions.memo: A lodge manager works in hospitality (accommodation), running a place where tourists stay.

questions.question: Why does tourism offer such a wide range of careers?
options: It covers many sectors — transport, hospitality, attractions, events and more
It only offers jobs in hotels
It has just one type of job
It offers no jobs at all
questions.expected: It covers many sectors — transport, hospitality, attractions, events and more
questions.memo: Tourism spans many sectors and sub-sectors, so it offers a wide variety of careers and opportunities.

questions.question: An air traffic controller and a coach driver both work in the _________ sector of tourism.
questions.memo: Both jobs help move or manage the movement of tourists, so they belong to the transport sector.

TOUR.G11.T4.REQUIREMENTS.A1.title: Requirements and inherent qualities to work in tourism
TOUR.G11.T4.REQUIREMENTS.A1.description: Identify the requirements and inherent qualities (personality type, characteristics and essential skills) needed to work in a particular tourism sector or career.
TOUR.G11.T4.REQUIREMENTS.A1.strand: Term 4 — Customer care, quality service and careers
TOUR.G11.T4.REQUIREMENTS.A1.caps_topic: Tourism sectors — requirements and inherent qualities to work in tourism
TOUR.G11.T4.REQUIREMENTS.A1.recovery_strategy: Match each job to the qualities and skills it most needs, one role at a time.

questions.question: Which quality is most important for a tour guide?
questions.memo: A tour guide must communicate clearly and engagingly to inform and entertain visitors, so good communication is essential.

questions.question: What is an 'inherent quality' in a tourism worker?
options: A natural personal characteristic, such as patience or friendliness
A piece of equipment they own
questions.expected: A natural personal characteristic, such as patience or friendliness
questions.memo: Inherent qualities are personal characteristics a person has, such as patience, friendliness and a positive attitude.

questions.question: A worker who deals with upset customers needs plenty of _________.
questions.memo: Patience helps a worker stay calm and helpful with difficult or upset customers.

questions.question: True or false: A friendly, positive attitude is an important quality for most tourism jobs.
questions.memo: Most tourism jobs involve dealing with people, so a friendly, positive attitude is important across the industry.

questions.question: Which skill is especially important for a chef?
questions.memo: A chef's key skills are preparing and cooking food to a high standard. Different jobs need different specific skills.

questions.question: Why is teamwork an important quality in tourism jobs?
options: Staff must work together to give guests a smooth experience
Staff should never speak to each other
Working alone always gives better service
questions.expected: Staff must work together to give guests a smooth experience
questions.memo: Tourism service depends on different staff working together, so teamwork helps deliver a smooth, good experience.

questions.question: A worker who speaks more than one _________ can help visitors from different countries.
questions.memo: Speaking more than one language is a valuable skill for serving international visitors.

questions.question: True or false: A tour guide needs good knowledge of the places and attractions they show visitors.
questions.memo: Guides must know the history, facts and stories of the attractions so they can inform and engage visitors.

questions.question: Which quality best suits a job that involves long hours on your feet helping guests?
options: A need to sit down all day
questions.memo: Active, people-facing jobs need stamina and energy to keep performing well throughout long shifts.

questions.question: Match each tourism job to a quality or skill it especially needs.
questions.memo: Guides need public-speaking and destination knowledge; chefs need cooking and hygiene skills; receptionists need friendly booking and phone skills.

questions.question: Why is reliability an important quality in a tourism worker?
options: Guests and colleagues depend on staff to do their jobs on time
It allows staff to skip work
It makes no difference to the service
questions.expected: Guests and colleagues depend on staff to do their jobs on time
questions.memo: Reliable staff can be counted on to be there and do their work, which keeps the service running smoothly.

questions.question: True or false: A receptionist needs good organisational and communication skills.
questions.memo: Receptionists juggle bookings, enquiries and guests, so they need to be organised and communicate well.

questions.question: A worker with good _________ skills can solve guests' problems calmly and well.
questions.memo: Problem-solving skills help staff handle issues and complaints calmly and find good solutions.

questions.question: Which personality type suits a front-of-house tourism job that involves constant contact with guests?
questions.memo: Front-of-house jobs suit outgoing, friendly people who enjoy interacting with guests.

questions.question: Why might a tour guide need to be flexible?
options: Plans can change due to weather, delays or group needs
So they never have to adapt
So they can refuse to change anything
Flexibility is never needed in tourism
questions.expected: Plans can change due to weather, delays or group needs
questions.memo: Tours often face changes — weather, delays, group requests — so guides must adapt their plans flexibly.

questions.question: Sort each item by whether it is a personal quality or a learned skill.
questions.memo: Patience, friendliness and a positive attitude are personal qualities. Cooking, using a booking system and speaking a language are learned skills.

questions.question: True or false: Attention to detail is a useful quality for a worker preparing travel documents.
questions.memo: Preparing documents and bookings requires accuracy, so attention to detail helps avoid costly mistakes.

questions.question: Which is an essential skill for a travel agent?
options: Using booking systems and knowing destinations well
questions.expected: Using booking systems and knowing destinations well
questions.memo: Travel agents must use booking systems and know destinations and products to advise and book for clients.

questions.question: Why should a worker choose a tourism career that suits their own interests and strengths?
options: They are likely to enjoy it and perform better
So they can dislike their job
So they avoid using their strengths
Interests have no effect on performance
questions.expected: They are likely to enjoy it and perform better
questions.memo: Matching a career to your interests and strengths means you enjoy the work more and do it better.

questions.question: Good _________ skills help tourism workers explain, listen and assist guests effectively.
questions.memo: Communication skills underpin nearly every tourism job, helping staff explain, listen and assist guests well.

TOUR.G11.T4.ENTREPRENEUR.A1.title: Entrepreneurial opportunities in tourism
TOUR.G11.T4.ENTREPRENEUR.A1.description: Explain the concept of an entrepreneur, the skills needed to be one, how to identify tourism products or services suitable for a business, and opportunities to start your own tourism business.
TOUR.G11.T4.ENTREPRENEUR.A1.strand: Term 4 — Customer care, quality service and careers
TOUR.G11.T4.ENTREPRENEUR.A1.caps_topic: Tourism sectors — entrepreneurial opportunities in tourism
TOUR.G11.T4.ENTREPRENEUR.A1.recovery_strategy: Link each entrepreneurial skill to a real tourism business idea, then judge one opportunity at a time.

questions.question: What is an entrepreneur?
options: A person who starts and runs their own business, taking on the risk
A person who only ever works for someone else
A person who refuses to take any risk
A government official who sets tax rates
questions.expected: A person who starts and runs their own business, taking on the risk
questions.memo: An entrepreneur spots an opportunity, starts a business and takes on the risk in the hope of making a profit.

questions.question: Which skill is important for an entrepreneur?
questions.memo: Entrepreneurs need to plan, manage money, make decisions and take initiative to run a successful business.

questions.question: An entrepreneur takes a _________ in the hope of making a profit.
questions.memo: Starting a business involves risk — money and effort could be lost — which the entrepreneur accepts in the hope of profit.

questions.question: True or false: Starting your own guided-tour business is an example of a tourism entrepreneurial opportunity.
questions.memo: Setting up your own guided-tour business is a clear example of an entrepreneurial opportunity in tourism.

questions.question: Which of these is a tourism business an entrepreneur could start?
questions.memo: A guesthouse is a tourism business an individual can start and run. The others are public or government bodies, not private tourism businesses.

questions.question: Why is creativity useful for a tourism entrepreneur?
options: It helps them think of new products and stand out from competitors
It stops them from ever finding ideas
It is not useful at all
questions.expected: It helps them think of new products and stand out from competitors
questions.memo: Creativity helps an entrepreneur come up with fresh, appealing products that set their business apart from others.

questions.question: Spotting a gap in the market means finding a need that is not yet being _________.
questions.memo: A gap in the market is a customer need that no business is yet meeting — an opportunity for an entrepreneur.

questions.question: True or false: An entrepreneur needs no planning and takes no risk.
questions.memo: Entrepreneurs must plan carefully and do take on risk — both are central to starting and running a business.

questions.question: Which is a tourism service an entrepreneur could offer?
questions.memo: An airport shuttle is a private tourism service an entrepreneur can run. The others are government functions.

questions.question: Sort each item by whether it is an entrepreneurial skill or quality.

items.text: Giving up at the first problem

questions.memo: Money management, creativity, risk-taking and determination help an entrepreneur. Giving up easily and refusing to plan do not.

questions.question: Why is determination important for an entrepreneur?
options: Starting a business is hard, so they must keep going through challenges
It helps them quit at the first setback
questions.expected: Starting a business is hard, so they must keep going through challenges
questions.memo: Building a business takes time and faces setbacks, so determination keeps an entrepreneur working towards success.

questions.question: True or false: A craft stall selling local souvenirs to tourists is an entrepreneurial opportunity.
questions.memo: A craft stall selling souvenirs is a small tourism business an entrepreneur can start and grow.

questions.question: An entrepreneur who identifies a tourist _________ that is not being met has found a business opportunity.
questions.memo: Finding an unmet tourist need is the starting point for a new product or service — a business opportunity.

questions.question: Why should an entrepreneur research the market before starting a tourism business?
options: To check there are enough customers and understand competitors
To make sure the business fails
questions.expected: To check there are enough customers and understand competitors
questions.memo: Market research shows whether there is demand and who the competitors are, helping the entrepreneur plan a viable business.

questions.question: Which is an example of an entrepreneur identifying a good opportunity?
options: Noticing tourists need transport from the airport and starting a shuttle
Copying a failing business with no changes
Starting a business with no customers in mind
questions.expected: Noticing tourists need transport from the airport and starting a shuttle
questions.memo: A good opportunity matches a real tourist need with a service — like spotting a transport gap and starting a shuttle.

questions.question: Sort each idea by whether it is a tourism business an entrepreneur could start.
questions.memo: Guesthouses, tour services and craft stalls are tourism businesses. Passport and tax offices are government functions, not private tourism businesses.

questions.question: True or false: Good communication and money-management skills both help an entrepreneur succeed.
questions.memo: Communication wins customers and partners, while money management keeps the business healthy — both help success.

questions.question: What does it mean to take a 'calculated risk'?
options: Taking a risk after weighing up the likely costs and benefits
Never taking any risk at all
questions.expected: Taking a risk after weighing up the likely costs and benefits
questions.memo: A calculated risk is taken thoughtfully, after considering the possible gains and losses — wiser than a reckless gamble.

questions.question: Why is a business plan useful to a tourism entrepreneur?
options: It sets out the goals, costs and steps to run the business
It guarantees there will be no competition
It removes the need for any customers
It is only for large companies, never small ones
questions.expected: It sets out the goals, costs and steps to run the business
questions.memo: A business plan maps the goals, costs, customers and steps, helping the entrepreneur stay organised and attract support.

questions.question: An _________ starts their own business to turn a tourism opportunity into a profit.
questions.memo: An entrepreneur is the person who starts and runs the business, taking the opportunity and the risk in the hope of profit.
